name: Chocolate Chip Cookie Dippin' Sticks with Milk

instructions.primary_message: Cut butter into small pieces. Place in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment, then set aside to soften, 10-15 minutes.
Meanwhile, place flour, baking soda, salt, and baking powder in a medium bowl, then whisk to combine the dry ingredients. Set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ¼ cups all-purpose flour
½ tsp baking soda
¼ tsp salt
⅛ tsp baking powder

instructions.primary_message: Once the butter has softened, beat on medium-high speed until light and creamy, 2-3 minutes. Stop the mixer and scrape down the sides of the bowl with a silicone spatula.
Add sugar to the bowl. Continue to mix on medium speed until the butter mixture is light in color and fluffy in texture, 3-5 minutes more. Stop the mixer and scrape down the sides of the bowl.
Add egg and vanilla to the bowl. Mix on medium speed until fully combined, about 2 minutes. Scrape down the sides of the bowl.

Add dry ingredients to the bowl. Mix on low speed until the cookie dough is just combined. Add chocolate chips and mix once more until evenly distributed. Cover the bowl, place in the fridge, and chill for 1 hour.
When the dough has chilled, line two large baking sheet pans with parchment paper.

Portion dough using a 1 oz cookie scoop or 2 tbsp measure. Working one by one, shape each portion into a 6-inch log, by rolling the dough with the palm of your hand on a cutting board. Arrange on the baking sheets, spaced apart by at least 2 inches (the cookies will spread as they bake).
Place baking sheets in the freezer until cookie dough is frozen, about 1 hour. (If desired, transfer the shaped cookie dough to a plastic bag and freeze until ready to bake at a later time.)
When you're ready to bake the cookies, preheat oven to 375°F.

Working in batches, place baking sheets in the preheated oven and bake until cookies are just set, about 10 minutes. Remove from oven and immediately use two spatulas to gently push in the sides and straighten the cookies into sticks while they're still soft. Let cool completely on the baking sheet. (It's best to bake in batches so that the cookies can be formed into sticks while still warm, before they cool down too much.)
Serve cookies with a glass of milk and enjoy!
